headline: US stocks closed lower as oil jumped on US‑Iran tensions, reviving inflation and Fed rate‑hike fears and pressuring tech and small caps
raw_text:
- S&P 500 (SPY), Dow Jones (DIA), Nasdaq Composite (QQQ) and Russell 2000 (IWM) all ended lower, with the Nasdaq leading declines and snapping a three‑day winning streak
- Crude oil (@CL) gained about 1% after renewed US‑Iran tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and President Trump’s vow to reinstate a naval blockade of Iranian ports
- Energy stocks outperformed on the oil move, with refiners such as Valero (VLO) rising
- Technology and semiconductor stocks lagged sharply, with Marvell (MRVL), Intel (INTC), Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU), Broadcom (AVGO) and AMD (AMD) falling on AI‑related spending concerns, geopolitical tensions and trade jitters
- SK Hynix (SKHY) American depositary shares dropped about 9% after reports that Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz triggered a sharp selloff in Korean and global chip stocks
- Defensive sectors including consumer staples and utilities held up relatively better than the broader market
- There was no major scheduled US economic data or large‑cap earnings driving Monday’s regular session
- Micro‑cap names VEEE (VEEE) and SOBR (SOBR) recorded outsized gains on company‑specific news, leading volatile penny‑stock moves
- Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled potential further rate hikes if inflation persists, adding to risk‑off sentiment
- Traders looked ahead to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s congressional testimony and Tuesday earnings from JPMorgan (JPM), Citigroup (C), Bank of America (BAC), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC) for fresh cues on rates and the economic outlook
